parts:
Here's a professional way to approach it that keeps the relationship strong, protects your culture, and leaves the door open:

---

**Hi Jenna,**

First, I want to thank you again for taking the time to speak with us. The more we get to know you, the more impressed we are by your experience, professionalism, and the value you could bring to The Luxora Collective.

As we've continued building out the company and evaluating our hiring structure, we've made some decisions around compensation and team alignment to ensure we're creating consistency across all sales roles. Because of that, we've standardized our closer compensation structure at **10% commission** for all closers moving forward.

I know we previously discussed a different percentage, and I wanted to be transparent with you as we've refined the business model. At this stage, we're still in the process of scaling lead flow and building a predictable volume of booked calls, so we're not yet in a position to offer a salaried role or guaranteed income.

That said, we genuinely believe you could be a tremendous asset to the company and would love to keep exploring ways you could be involved as we continue to grow. Before making any long-term decisions, we'd still love for you to complete the Cultural Index assessment. Beyond sales, we're always looking at where exceptional people may fit within the organization as we build out the team.

Most importantly, this is not a reflection of how highly we think of you. Quite the opposite. We see a lot of potential and would love to continue the conversation as the company grows and additional opportunities become available.

Thank you again for your time, and we look forward to staying connected.

**Bethany Gifford**  
Founder & CEO  
urlThe Luxora Collectivehttps://theluxoracollective.co/

---

This positions it as a business-model decision rather than a rejection, keeps her engaged with the Cultural Index, and avoids making promises while preserving the relationship for future opportunities.

I would frame it around **company growth, standardization, and opportunity**, not around "we can't pay you" or "we changed our minds."

:::writing{variant="chat_message" id="58341"}
Hi Jenna,

I wanted to follow up and give you a transparent update on where we are as a company.

First, we think very highly of you and would absolutely love to have you involved with The Luxora Collective. As we've continued building the sales team, we've spent a lot of time refining our compensation structure, onboarding process, and long-term growth plan.

As a result, we've standardized all closer compensation at 10% commission across the board. I know we originally discussed a higher percentage, but since then we've increased our program pricing, so the earning potential is actually very comparable to what we initially discussed.

We're also currently interviewing several candidates and running everyone through the same process to ensure we're building the right team and culture from the start. That includes completing the Cultural Index assessment and having candidates pitch our offer so we can evaluate communication style, sales ability, and overall fit.

In addition, we've partnered with a sales training and onboarding team that will be helping whichever closer we ultimately bring on board get up to speed quickly with our GHL systems, sales process, and overall workflow. We want to make sure whoever joins us has the support, training, and resources needed to succeed from day one.

We're still in the process of building predictable call volume and scaling lead flow, so we're being very intentional about every hire we make. That said, we see a lot of value in what you bring to the table and would love for you to continue through the process by completing the Cultural Index so we can explore where you may be the best fit within the organization as we continue to grow.

Thank you again for your time and interest in what we're building. We truly appreciate it and look forward to continuing the conversation.

Bethany
:::

This keeps her feeling wanted, explains the compensation change without apologizing for it, and positions the Cultural Index as part of a professional hiring process rather than a consolation prize.
